title: The role fallback gives assault to units no role step reaches
reason:
Step 5 is the generalist step for units that fight. A unit that cannot fight, and whose main action fits none of step 2's roles, needs its own last step, and the fix supplies one: the closest role whose requires the unit meets, plus a fit_note. It is written as a condition on step 5 (a weapon that is not a tool, the term item 25 defines) and a new step 6. Assault's coding rule gets a matching clause, so its 'As primary: any generalist' sentence cannot be read as barring assault at step 6 (the M.A.D. Tank). The alternative is not recommended. Adding jobs to the word list (ships as an anti-armour target, a concealment role) brings in terms the cards and generator would also need, and the entry's specific causes have their own items: 21 for ability damage, and 38 and 39 (not in this round) for beam artillery and armed workers. I checked all 28 units: only the two unarmed units that reach step 5 today change path. The Submarine, Magnetron, Slave Miner and Chrono Legionnaire are armed, so step 5 still gives them assault or raider and their fit_notes stay. Tested in a scratch copy together with all the other edits: format, validate, docs build and all 284 tests pass. The Gap Generator's flavour_affinity, recomputed with buffer, stays allied.

Not confirmed as drafted; the skeptic's corrected form is used (edits from the verdict, recodes from the verdict). Skeptic: The rule is right in substance. Of the units that reach step 5 today, only the Gap Generator changes value. The M.A.D. Tank keeps assault, now through step 6. The armed fallback units (Submarine, Magnetron, Slave Miner, Chrono Legionnaire) keep their step-5 roles. Flavour stays [allied]. Buffer as the closest fit holds up as a judgement: buffer has no requires. Scout's requires are met through shroud-area's stealth-deception category, but its description and the buffer/scout tie-break point away from it. Support, area denial and disabler fail their requires, and raider needs a weapon. For the M.A.D. Tank, assault is the closest role whose requires it meets; anti-armour, siege, disabler and area denial all fail theirs.

The draft has three gaps.
(1) Step 6's own condition is too narrow. 'With a main button or main action that fits none of step 2's roles' is not step 2's test, which needs a role that fits AND has its requires met. The Gap Generator's action fits support (its fit_note asks for support), but support's requires fail. Read strictly, step 6 then does not cover the truck, and it gets no role at all. Corrected wording: 'and step 2 found no role for its main button or main action'.
(2) The Gap Generator recode breaks a validator test. The categoryRole helper in tests/validate.test.mjs looks for 'a rule-free role nobody has' but reads only data/units/ra3.json. It therefore picks buffer, adds a requires to it, and the RA1 truck then fails that requires. The fix is to have the helper read every data/units file; it then picks engineer. The analyst's 'all 284 tests pass' held only without the recodes.
(3) The Gap Generator is a checked unit, and roles/primary is in its review/checked_paths. House practice takes a field that changed after the check out of checked_paths and names it in review/notes.

One small polish to the assault coding rule: 'no earlier step reaches', since step 6 itself does reach the unit.

title: Anti-armour's requires shut out units the sources call tank killers
reason: Requires are a gate on a unit's parts. The validator matches them against weapons and patterns, and the generator's cards must meet the same requires with parts. A source unit that met anti-armour through praise would claim a role that no card with the same parts could claim, and the validator could not check it. The pilot chose this hard gate plus fit_notes on purpose (research/pilot/round-1/analysis/identity.json). The fix would also miss two of the three units. The Magnetron's official texts have no strong-against line about vehicles (they say it lifts and pulls them). The Mastermind's anti-vehicle is a word in its role line, which item 18 handles: anti-armour is skipped because it fails its requires. The Kirov's case is a damage question: its profile calls the bombs armour-piercing, while RA3's damage map reads their Explosive category as explosive. That belongs to the damage rules (weapons group). If its bombs were recoded armour-piercing, anti-armour would follow from the existing tests, since the profile says one airship can wreck an armour force. The three units' fit_notes already carry the wanted role to the next word-list review, as designed.

title: Hedged wording in the role tests
reason: This takes only the hedge rule from the fix, as one sentence in the roles word list. The word list already says which words count, so the sentence covers every test that reads words to give a role: role lines at step 1, step 4's strong-against text, roles.secondary's 'a source calls it an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon', and roles.secondary step 1. A hedge on whether the unit or weapon does the job at all no longer counts. A hedge on how much it destroys still counts, so the Yak's line that a run may wipe out a whole group keeps it anti-infantry. That alone removes the Siege Chopper's anti-air, whose only support is the wiki's hedged line. The other two parts of the fix are left out. First, widening the drop rule to any cited source would let wiki and guide weakness lines remove roles across the batch. The drop rule reads only official text by design, the RA1 notes keep StrategyWiki out of it, and the Siege Chopper does not need it. Second, the anti-air trait follows can_target by its coding rule ('set it exactly when its can_target includes high-air'). Dropping the trait while high air stays would make the machine gun break machine-gun's allowed targets (no high air) and need an atypical entry. The gun does fire at high fliers, weakly, so the trait is a weapon question for the weapons group. A scan of every unit's role notes and weapon summaries found no other role resting on hedged words.

title: The role steps read only weapons, so damaging abilities earn no role
reason:
The broad fix is not recommended. Letting any damaging ability give roles the way a weapon does also hands roles to buttons that hit everything: the Spy's earned parabomb strike, coded as one of its active abilities, would pass the splash test for anti-infantry. It also needs the validator to read summaries, and it reverses the pilot's deliberate choice to keep ability-fired anti-tank tools out of anti-armour (research/pilot/round-1/analysis/identity.json). Yet roles.secondary step 5 already lets an upgrade part meet a role's requires, while a stock button at step 2, which every copy has, cannot. So the narrow change puts step 2 on the same footing as step 5, and only for the strict anti tests: a button that harms only one kind of target, or that a source calls an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon. The validator cannot see a button's damage, so the unit records the role in atypical, as the climb trait's coding rule already does for a break the rules accept. Of the units with damaging buttons, only the Allied Minelayer changes. The M.A.D. Tank's pulse hits vehicles, ships, aircraft and buildings, and the parabombs, the Desolator's field and the Sickle's jump landing hit more than one kind of target. The Soviet Minelayer's anti-personnel mine already gives anti-infantry, which has no requires. Tested in the scratch copy: the Allied Minelayer with secondary anti-armour fails validation without the atypical entry and passes with it.

Not confirmed as drafted; the skeptic's corrected form is used (edits from the verdict, recodes from the verdict). Skeptic: The drafted recode is wrong.

The Allied Minelayer's mine button does support anti-armour: only vehicles set the mines off, and the manual calls them AT Mines. But anti-armour's requires check damage, and these mines do HE damage. EA's UNIT.CPP has a vehicle that drives over an AV mine take Rule.AVMineDamage with WARHEAD_HE, and the RA1 damage map reads HE as explosive. Anti-armour needs armour-piercing, energy, electric or EMP damage, or infest-vehicle, so its requires fail 'as at step 5' and roles/secondary stays empty.

The analyst read 'meet its requires through the button' as met by the button being anti-tank. The drafted sentence invites that reading, which would quietly bring back the praise-based route that item 10 rejects. The corrected wording says the button's damage and targets are read as for a weapon, which keeps requires based on parts.

With that, item 21 changes no R1 value. Neither unit in entry 21 gets anti-armour: the M.A.D. Tank's pulse hits four kinds of target, and the Minelayer's mines are explosive. Mustafa may prefer to drop the item, or keep it for later buttons whose damage does meet a requires.

The two Minelayer notes must still change: their reason, that an ability cannot meet requires, is no longer what the rule says. The drafted atypical entry, sources/0/supports change and fit_note removal are not needed. Had the role been added, roles/secondary and sources/0/supports are in this checked unit's review/checked_paths and would have had to leave it; the draft missed that as well.

title: The RA1 and RA2 notes differ on which words count for roles
reason:
One rule now lives in the roles word list for every game. Any word form of a label or alias counts, only when it describes the unit's own job, which the RA1 notes already require and which word forms make necessary (an enemy's anti-aircraft fire must not name anti-air). A unit's name counts only when it names the unit's job. The three games' notes are aligned with it. RA1 drops 'never counts'. RA2 limits the counted name to a job name and gives the Siege Chopper's 'harass' as a word-form example. RA3 moves the Spy's Infiltration to the words that name infiltrator (the RA3 Spy is not an R1 unit). The alternative is not recommended: it would strip step-1 roles from RA2's Engineer, Spy, Tank Destroyer and miners. I scanned every R1 unit's official texts for word forms and job names. Only the Siege Chopper's ranking changes. The RA1 Spy now gets infiltrator at step 1 instead of step 2, the two Minelayers get area denial at step 1 (Mine Layer), and the Slave Miner keeps logistics at secondary step 1 because its name names its job: same values. Tanya's 'marksmanship' fails marksman's requires, and the Robot Tank's 'raider' fails raider's speed requires, as before.

title: No link kinds for price, availability or immunity
reason:
Link kinds are field rules: x-ref-kinds and the ref pattern in schemas/common.schema.json, plus one sentence in the Typed links convention. The validator must also resolve and match the new kinds (with tests), and the three R1 notes that tell coders to 'say so in strengths' should name the link. The fix is right: tier:t1, tier:t3 and class:infantry claim a tech level or a class when the reason is about price, a cap or an immunity. Choices: cost is ranked (cost-bands already has ranks), so a group can be named (cost:<=low). availability is unranked. immune takes a damage type, a pattern id or a mobility trait (immune:toxic, immune:mind-control, immune:crush, immune:infest-vehicle), which covers every immunity R1 met. A part keeps the link only when the word lists themselves make it immune (an uncrewed machine against psionic and toxic attacks, in the nature and damage-type lists). That is checkable, keeps the Robot Tank's and Chaos Drone's nature links, and stops a job or mobility standing in for a game rule (miners, fliers). tier stays for reasons about tech, so the Hammer Tank sample's 'Needs a Super Reactor' keeps tier:t2. The validator matches cost against a unit's cost_band.band and a card's balance.cost_band. The own-parts check skips immune links, since no profile records immunities; on a card, an immune strength fails the own-parts check, which fits the rule that a card's immunity comes from its parts. The Sickle's and Kirov's price entries were dropped in R1, so they have nothing to recode.

Not confirmed as drafted; the skeptic's corrected form is used (edits from the draft, recodes from the verdict). Skeptic: The edits are right and do no more than the fix needs. They add cost:, availability: and immune: to x-ref-kinds and to the ref pattern. The validator resolves an immune id as a damage type, a mobility trait or a pattern. It matches cost against a unit's cost_band.band or a card's balance.cost_band, and availability against availability. Only the unit own-parts check skips immune links. The card check (`if (!matches(r.ref, P))`) still runs, so an immune strength on a card fails, as the draft says. Nothing clashes with another rule: tier: stays for tech (the Hammer Tank sample's weaknesses/3 tier:t2 is the only tier link left in units and patterns), the example card has no affected link, and the Typed links sentence is separate from the Matchups string that 19, 28 and 36 change. Every drafted recode matches the data and the new rule. Bands checked: Attack Dog very-low, Field Mechanic medium, M.A.D. Tank very-high, Mammoth high, Chrono Legionnaire very-high, Mastermind very-high, Sudden Transport and Terror Drone low; Boris and Tanya are unique. The Boris sources/1 and fit_notes changes and the Legionnaire and Desolator fit_notes changes are right. The recode list is incomplete, though: two immunities that the edited notes name still sit on other links. (a) Slave Miner strengths/0 (armour-class:heavy) says 'unharmed by radiation'. The edited radiation note names the Slave Miner (not its Slaves) for immune:toxic, and its wiki page (sources/1) says the miner is immune while the Slaves die in irradiated ground. (b) Mastermind strengths/0 (pattern:mind-control) ends with 'enemy mind control cannot take it in return'. The mind-control note lists Masterminds as immune and now says an immune unit links immune:mind-control, and its wiki infobox (sources/2) gives the immunity. pattern:mind-control says the unit does mind control, not that it resists it. Both are split the way the draft splits Boris: trim the old reason and append an immune entry. Because the entry is appended, no index moves. sources/1 (Slave Miner) and sources/2 (Mastermind) support all of strengths, and no fit note records either gap, so neither needs a supports or fit_notes change. The validator cannot catch these, because an immunity named inside a reason is invisible to it. The corrected list is the drafted one plus four rows. After applying, run npm run docs: the edits leave docs/fields.md stale, and the Terror Drone sample recode leaves docs/samples.md stale. This is expected for generated pages.

title: Matchups rule 3: unit links
reason:
A field rule (Matchups rule 3). Two parts of the fix are taken as proposed: something only one kind of unit makes names that unit (minefields name the Minelayers), and a lone unit link says so in its reason. The trigger is narrowed. Almost every word-list link covers some units its reason is false for, so 'every word-list link would cover units the reason is false for' would let unit links stand alone nearly always and undo rule 3. Here a lone link needs every word-list and pattern link to be false for most of the units it covers (Boris: crush covers every crusher, and only the Battle Fortress crushes heroes). A link false for only a few keeps its place and names them: the Cryocopter's armour-class:>=heavy already names the Kirov, and its role:siege now names the bombers and airships. Boris's countered_by/1 already says 'the one vehicle that can crush heroes', so it needs no change; it is the only lone unit link in R1. The Yak page names minefields, not the Minelayer, and both minelayers already list the Yak in countered_by/1, so the Yak gains the matching counters.

Not confirmed as drafted; the skeptic's corrected form is used (edits from the verdict, recodes from the verdict). Skeptic: Most of the draft is right. The minefield clause and the narrowed lone-link trigger ('false for most of the units it covers') do what the fix needs and keep rule 3 meaningful. Boris's countered_by/1 is the only lone unit link in R1, and its reason already says the Battle Fortress is the one vehicle that crushes heroes. The Yak recodes are right: the Yak page says a force-fire order clears any mines in the area, both minelayers already list the Yak at countered_by/1, and sources/1 is updated. The last clause, 'when a link is false for only a few units, keep it and name them in the reason', is the problem. It adds a naming duty that goes far beyond the fix and beyond the recode list. By the draft's own reasoning, almost every word-list link covers some units its reason is false for, yet the list names only the Cryocopter's role:siege. Unnamed exceptions remain all over R1. For example, the Mastermind's countered_by/1 nature:uncrewed-machine also covers the unarmed Chaos Drone. The class:aircraft entries in countered_by ('aircraft attack it freely' on the Minelayers, Desolator, Robot Tank, Chrono Legionnaire and others) also cover fliers with no weapon, such as RA1's transport helicopter. Either the list grows into a survey of every link, or the clause stops asking for names. The smaller change keeps the half the fix needs: such a link stays, so a unit link may not stand alone beside it. It drops the naming duty. The Cryocopter recode is then unnecessary: its counters/0 already names the Kirov, and its counters/1 already says ground artillery. The drafted text is harmless but not needed, so I drop it to keep the change small.

title: Weapon labels: when can_target step 3 applies, and whether it lists structures
reason:
This is the proposed fix with one change. The label is defined once, in can_target step 3, and roles.secondary now points to that definition. A label is any wording in any source, guides included, that names the weapon by its job or by its targets: a heading, a wiki's anti-tank gun, or a target line such as Target: Naval. Words about what the weapon is good at are not a label, and neither is a label on the unit. A sentence that only says what the weapon cannot hit removes that kind, and step 4 fills in the rest. Under step 3, wording of the weapon's own that says ground or surface counts as the sources saying it damages buildings. That wording can be a label such as anti-surface, a guide's Target: Ground, or an infobox ground attack line that names the weapon or belongs to the unit's only weapon. A label that names only other kinds (anti-armour, anti-infantry) does not count. This was the RA1 reconciler's proposal, and it named the infobox line itself. The infobox line adds structures and nothing else, so the RA1 Submarine's torpedoes, which sit on a ground attack line, do not gain infantry or vehicles. The one change from the fix: a label on another unit's copy of the weapon counts when a source says that copy has the same stats. The Multigunner IFV page labels its Tanya gun anti-infantry and says it has the same stats as her own weapons, and StrategyWiki says that copy engages only infantry. Under the fix as written, Tanya's pistols would fall to step 4 and list vehicles, buildings and ships, while every source pairs the pistols with infantry and her charges with the rest. Tanya's infobox gives one unit-wide ground attack line for two weapons, so it adds nothing. To take the fix exactly as proposed, drop the words 'unless a source says that copy has the same stats'. Tanya's armament/0/can_target then becomes [infantry, ground-vehicle, structure, naval]. Audit of all 28 units: the Mammoth (StrategyWiki: anti-armor cannons, Target: Ground), the Yak (Target: Ground), the Submarine (Target: Naval plus the naval-yard text), the Desolator (cannot damage buildings), the dog, Boris, the Sickle, the Mecha Tengu, the Kirov, the Cryocopter, the step 1 weapons and every IFV passenger weapon keep their lists. The IFV's anti-surface shotgun and Tesla gun keep structures, and its anti-infantry laser still has none. The roles.secondary label clause still holds for the Mammoth's anti-armour (StrategyWiki heading) and the Siege Chopper's anti-air (the wiki says the gun also serves against aircraft). Tested in a scratch copy with every group edit and recode applied: validate, format, docs and tests all pass; only the vocab-diff test fails, as it always does in a copy.
